s: Who among the following issued coins bearing the image of Lakshmi?
x: Lakshmi appears on Muhammad Ghori's coins.

s: Unlike Mahmud of Ghazni, who mainly raided for plunder, what did Muhammad Ghori aim at?
x: Mahmud was mainly a plunder-seeking raider, while Ghori pursued conquest and a lasting political presence in North India.

s: Which was the first of Muhammad Ghori's conquests in India, taken in 1175?
x: Ghori took Multan in 1175, then Peshawar (c. 1179), Sindh (c. 1182) and Punjab and Lahore (c. 1190).

s: Who founded the Delhi Sultanate in 1206 after the death of Muhammad Ghori?
x: Qutbuddin Aibak, Ghori's slave and Master of Stables, founded the Delhi Sultanate in 1206.

s: Regarding Muhammad Ghori's Gujarat campaign, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Mularaja II – Area near which the battle of Kasahrada was fought
Mount Abu – Queen mother who acted as regent
x: Ghori's Gujarat campaign came in 1178, when Mularaja II, with his mother Naika Devi as regent, defeated him at Kasahrada near Mount Abu.

s: Muhammad Ghori entered India through which pass?
x: Muhammad Ghori entered India through the Gomal Pass.

s: In which year was the Second Battle of Tarain fought?
x: The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in 1192, the First in 1191, both against Prithviraj Chauhan.

s: Over which place did the First Battle of Tarain (1191) arise?
x: Tabarhinda (Bhatinda) was the cause; Prithviraj Chauhan won and Ghori barely escaped.

s: When Mularaja II defeated Muhammad Ghori in 1178, who acted as his regent?
x: Mularaja II (Bhimdev II) was a minor; his mother Naika Devi was regent when Ghori suffered his first defeat near Mount Abu.

s: Near which place was the Battle of Chandawar (1194) fought?
x: Chandawar lies near Firozabad (UP), on the Yamuna near Agra; Tarain is near Karnal.

s: At which battle was Jayachandra (Jaichand) of Kannauj defeated by Muhammad Ghori?
x: Ghori defeated Jayachandra at Chandawar (1194), near the Yamuna.

s: Who won the First Battle of Tarain in 1191?
x: In the First Battle of Tarain (1191) Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori, who barely escaped. Ghori won the second battle in 1192.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Battle)
A. First Tarain (1191)
B. Second Tarain (1192)
C. Chandawar (1194)
D. Kasahrada near Mount Abu (1178)
List-II (Result)
1. Muhammad Ghori defeated Jaichand
2. Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori
3. Mularaja II defeated Muhammad Ghori
4. Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Prithviraj won Tarain I (1191) and lost Tarain II (1192); Ghori beat Jaichand at Chandawar (1194); Mularaja II of Gujarat gave Ghori his first defeat in 1178.

s: Tarain, where Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad Ghori fought in 1191 and 1192, lies near Karnal in which present state?
x: Tarain is near Karnal in Haryana.

s: Which of the following places was NOT among those captured by Muhammad bin Qasim?
x: Muhammad bin Qasim captured Debal, Nirun, Sehwan, Brahmanabad and Multan. Somnath was attacked much later by Mahmud of Ghazni.

s: Which was the capital of Raja Dahir, who was defeated by Muhammad bin Qasim in 712 CE?
x: Dahir's capital was Alor (Aror); Brahmanabad was only one of the places taken.

s: Who among the following repelled the Arab forces and thereby helped prevent their expansion beyond Sindh?
x: Nagabhata I repelled the Arabs. Arab writers also noted that the Pratiharas possessed the most formidable cavalry in India.

s: After the Arab conquest of Sindh, Hindus and Buddhists were given which status?
x: The conquest did not cause mass Islamisation; Hindus and Buddhists were granted dhimmi status.

s: Which of the following did NOT confine Arab rule to Sindh?
o: Complete political unity in North India
The strength of the Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas and Palas
x: North India was not completely united; geography, strong regional states and weak resources restricted the Arabs.

s: Which of the following was one of the important contributions transmitted from India to the Islamic world and subsequently to Europe?
x: Indian mathematics, especially the decimal and place-value systems, along with astronomy and medicine, passed to the Islamic world and later to Europe.

s: Whose nephew and son-in-law was Muhammad bin Qasim?
x: Qasim was the nephew and son-in-law of Al-Hajjaj, the Umayyad governor; Caliph al-Walid sent him.

s: Arab writers said which Indian dynasty had the strongest cavalry in India?
x: Arab writers credited the Pratiharas, whose Nagabhata I drove back the Arabs, with the strongest cavalry.

s: Who translated the Chachnama into Persian?
o: Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi
x: The Chachnama, the chronicle of the Arab conquest of Sindh, was translated into Persian by Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi.

s: Which Umayyad Caliph sent Muhammad bin Qasim to conquer Sindh?
x: Muhammad bin Qasim was sent by Caliph al-Walid, at the age of 17, through the governor Al-Hajjaj.

s: What is the Chachnama, translated into Persian by Kufi, a chronicle of?
x: The Chachnama is an Arabic chronicle of the conquest of Sindh (680-718), later translated into Persian by Kufi.

s: Which of the following was a cause of the Arab invasion of Sindh?
x: Arab maritime interests and piracy against Arab ships were among the causes of the conquest of Sindh.

s: How many times did Mahmud of Ghazni invade India between 1000 and 1027?
x: Mahmud raided India 17 times between 1000 and 1027.

s: Who resisted Mahmud of Ghazni among the following?
x: Chandela ruler Vidyadhara resisted Mahmud of Ghazni.

s: Under pressure from whom did the Ghaznavids decline after Mahmud?
x: The Ghaznavid power declined after Mahmud under Seljuk pressure.

s: Which one of the following statements about Mahmud's campaigns is correct?
o: The Pratihara ruler of Kanauj resisted him successfully throughout.
Somnath was attacked in 1025 when Bhima I of the Solanki line was ruling Gujarat.
Nagarkot was attacked in 1194 during Ghori's campaign.
Mahmud attacked Somnath in 1009 under the rule of Jaichand.
x: Mahmud attacked Somnath in 1025, when the Solanki Bhima I ruled Gujarat. The other statements are wrong: the Pratihara king of Kanauj submitted to Mahmud and did not resist; Mahmud attacked Nagarkot in 1009, not Ghori in 1194; and Jaichand was the Gahadavala king of Kanauj whom Ghori defeated at Chandawar in 1194.

s: Which statement correctly describes the foundation of the Ghaznavid line?
o: Mahmud founded the line after the conquest of Somnath.
Alptigin and Sabuktigin were both rulers of the Ghurid dynasty.
Sabuktigin founded the line, while Alptigin was only a later governor.
Alptigin founded the line, while Sabuktigin is regarded as its real founder.
x: The Ghaznavid line was founded by Alptigin, while Sabuktigin is considered its real founder.

s: In which year did Mahmud of Ghazni raid the Chakraswamin temple at Thanesar?
x: Thanesar was raided in 1014; Mathura was sacked in 1018 and Somnath raided in 1025–26.

s: Somnath Swabhiman Parv was launched in January 2026 to commemorate which historical event?
o: Muhammad Ghori's victory in the Battle of Chandawar
Mahmud of Ghazni's attack on Somnath, a thousand years earlier
The Arab conquest of Sindh by Muhammad bin Qasim
x: Somnath Swabhiman Parv was launched in January 2026 to mark 1,000 years since Mahmud of Ghazni's attack on Somnath.

s: In which year did Mahmud of Ghazni raid Nagarkot (Kangra) for its temple treasure?
x: Mahmud raided Nagarkot in 1009; Thanesar was 1014, Mathura and Kanauj 1018, Somnath 1025-26.

s: At which place did the Pratihara king submit to Mahmud of Ghazni in 1018?
x: At Kanauj (1018) the Pratihara king submitted to Mahmud.

s: During the reign of which Solanki ruler was Somnath sacked by Mahmud in 1025-26?
x: The Somnath raid took place under Solanki Bhima I, not Bhima II; Mularaja II later defeated Ghori in 1178.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ghaznavids:
1. Alptigin was the founder of the Ghaznavid line.
2. Sabuktigin is called the real founder of the dynasty.
3. Mahmud aimed at a permanent empire in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Alptigin was the founder and Sabuktigin the real founder; Mahmud's raids were for plunder, not for a permanent empire.

s: Which Hindu Shahi rulers were the first to resist Mahmud of Ghazni?
x: Jayapala and Anandapala of the Hindu Shahi dynasty were the first to resist Mahmud.

s: Who wrote Tarikh-i-Subuktigin?
x: Baihaqi wrote Tarikh-i-Subuktigin; Utbi wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini and Al-Biruni Kitab-ul-Hind.

s: Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind is an objective account of India in which century?
x: Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind is an objective account of eleventh-century India.

s: What is the title of Al-Biruni's Arabic translation of Patanjali's Yoga-Sutra?
x: Al-Biruni translated the Yoga-Sutra into Arabic as Kitab Patanjal.

s: Who was the poet laureate (Malik-ush-Shuara) of Mahmud Ghaznavi's court?
x: Unsuri was poet laureate; Firdausi wrote the Shahnama and Utbi Kitab-ul-Yamini.

s: Who translated Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind into English?
x: Edward Sachau translated Kitab-ul-Hind into English.

s: Which work was written by Utbi, the court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni?
x: Utbi wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini (Tarikh-i-Yamini); Baihaqi wrote Tarikh-i-Subuktigin and Firdausi the Shahnama.

s: Who among the following court poets of Mahmud of Ghazni is called the 'Homer of the East'?
x: Firdausi, author of the Shahnama, is called the 'Homer of the East'.

s: Who wrote Taj-ul-Maasir?
x: Taj-ul-Maasir is by Hasan Nizami; Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.

s: Who wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri?
x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is the work of Minhaj-us-Siraj.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Taj-ul-Maasir was written by Hasan Nizami, not Minhaj-us-Siraj; the other pairs are correct.

s: The fragmentation of Rajput states that aided the Turks followed the collapse of which dynasty?
x: After the Pratiharas collapsed, Rajput states fragmented and competed, and this disunity helped the Turks.

s: Which historian linked Turkish success to 'Indian feudalism' - feudal levies, sub-infeudation and a closed village economy?
x: R.S. Sharma linked feudal levies, sub-infeudation and a closed village economy to Turkish success; caste also restricted fighting to a few groups.

s: Which one of the following was a military reason for Turkish success in North India?
o: Reliance on war elephants and slow infantry formations
Complete absence of cavalry in Turkish armies
x: Turkish armies used mobile cavalry and mounted archers, whereas Indian armies relied heavily on elephants.

s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of Turkish success:
1. North India lacked political unity after the Pratihara collapse.
2. The Turks relied on mounted archers against elephant-reliant Indian armies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: rival Rajput states lacked unity, and mobile cavalry with mounted archers beat elephant-based armies.

s: Who entered Nadiya, drove Lakshman Sen to East Bengal and captured Lakhnauti?
x: Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji entered Nadiya in 1204, drove Lakshmana Sena to East Bengal and ruled from Lakhnauti, after conquering Bihar.

s: Who was the real founder of Turk rule in Bihar?
x: Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji was the real founder of Turk rule in Bihar.

s: Which set of Buddhist centres was sacked by Bakhtiyar Khalji around 1193–1203?
x: Bakhtiyar Khalji sacked the Buddhist centres of Nalanda, Vikramashila and Odantapuri during approximately 1193–1203.

s: Which of the following dynasty–capital pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Solankis ruled from Anhilwada; the Gurjara-Pratiharas from Kannauj, the Paramaras from Dhara and the Kalachuris from Tripuri.

s: Who founded the Solanki (Chalukya) dynasty of Gujarat with its capital at Anhilwada?
x: Mularaja I founded the Solanki line, with its capital at Anhilwada (Patan).

s: Which Solanki ruler built the Modhera Sun temple?
x: Bhima I built the Modhera Sun temple; Somnath was sacked in 1025 during his reign.

s: Which ruler is correctly matched with the Sahasralinga tank at Patan and patronage of Hemachandra?
x: Jayasimha Siddharaja patronised the Jain scholar Hemachandra and is associated with the Sahasralinga tank at Patan.

s: Under whose influence did Kumarapala encourage Jainism?
x: Kumarapala encouraged Jainism under Hemachandra's influence; he also rebuilt Somnath and curbed animal slaughter.

s: In memory of whom did Udayamati build Rani-ki-Vav at Patan?
x: Rani-ki-Vav was built by Udayamati, queen of Bhima I, in his memory.

s: Which Solanki ruler, a Jain disciple of Hemachandra, rebuilt the Somnath temple?
x: Kumarapala (1143-1172), a disciple of Hemachandra, rebuilt Somnath.

s: Which one of the following statements about Somnath is correct?
o: It is a Vaishnava temple in Madhya Pradesh
It was rebuilt in the Chalukya era and is dedicated to Shiva as a jyotirlinga
Its present temple was completed in 1299 immediately after Khalji’s attack
The Old Somnath temple was built by Vimal Shah in 1031
x: Somnath is a Shiva temple and jyotirlinga in Gujarat. It was rebuilt in the Chalukya era, while the present temple was completed in 1951; Ahilyabai Holkar built the Old Somnath temple in 1783.

s: Modhera, site of the Solanki Sun temple, is in the news because it:
o: Was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2022
Was fully solarised under an MNRE scheme, inaugurated on 9 October 2022
Was declared a Hindu temple by the Gujarat High Court
Became the site of the Somnath Swabhiman Parv
x: Modhera was fully solarised under an MNRE scheme (6 MW plant with 15 MWh storage), inaugurated on 9 October 2022. The court ruling on a temple concerned Bhojshala (MP High Court); Somnath Swabhiman Parv concerns Somnath; there was no 2022 UNESCO listing for Modhera.

s: To whom is the Vimal Vasahi temple at Dilwara dedicated?
x: Vimal Vasahi (c. 1031) is dedicated to Rishabha; Luna Vasahi is dedicated to Neminatha.

s: Who built the Luna Vasahi temple at Dilwara (1230)?
x: Luna Vasahi was built by the Vaghela ministers Vastupala and Tejpal; Vimal Shah built Vimal Vasahi.

s: Who built the 'Old Somnath' temple in 1783?
x: Ahilyabai Holkar built Old Somnath in 1783; the present temple dates from 1951.

s: Who built the Vimal Vasahi temple at Dilwara, Mount Abu, around 1031?
x: Vimal Vasahi was built by Vimal Shah, minister of Solanki Bhima I, c. 1031.

s: In which year was the present Somnath temple built?
x: The present Somnath temple dates from 1951; Ahilyabai Holkar built 'Old Somnath' in 1783.

s: With which dynasty are Khajuraho and Mahoba in Bundelkhand associated?
x: The Chandelas held Bundelkhand with Khajuraho and Mahoba; the Paramaras held Malwa and the Gahadavalas Kanauj and Varanasi.

s: To which deity is the Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho dedicated?
x: Kandariya Mahadeva (by Vidyadhara) is a Shiva temple; the Lakshmana temple is Vishnu's.

s: In which district of Madhya Pradesh is the Khajuraho group of temples located?
x: The Khajuraho group (UNESCO), built by the Chandelas in 950-1050 CE, is in Chhatarpur district.

s: Which Chandela ruler built the Kandariya Mahadeva temple, the largest temple at Khajuraho?
x: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple was built by Vidyadhara.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding theories of Rajput origin and their proponents?
x: The foreign-origin theory, which associates the Rajputs with Scythians, Hunas and Gurjaras, was propounded by Col. James Tod and V.A. Smith. G.H. Ojha and C.V. Vaidya supported the Kshatriya-descent theory, while the Agnikula tradition is associated with Chand Bardai’s Prithviraj Raso.

s: The rise of the Chauhans of Ajmer, Chandelas of Bundelkhand and Paramaras of Malwa is principally associated with which event?
x: These Rajput states rose after the collapse of the Pratihara Empire, which led to political fragmentation in North India.

s: Which clan, along with the Paramara, Pratihara and Chauhan, makes up the traditional four Agnikula Rajput clans?
x: The four Agnikula clans are Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan and Solanki; the Chandelas are not on the traditional list.

s: Which scholar supported the Kshatriya descent theory of Rajput origin?
x: G.H. Ojha and C.V. Vaidya held the Kshatriya descent theory; Tod and Smith gave the foreign origin theory, Chand Bardai the Agnikula legend.

s: From where did the Tomaras, whose coins carried a horseman-and-bull motif, rule?
x: The Tomaras held Dhillika (Delhi); the Mehrauli Iron Pillar is a Gupta work only moved there.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Paramara dynasty was founded by Upendra, also known as Krishnaraja. Anangapala founded the Tomara dynasty.

s: Which was the capital of the Kalachuris (Chedis)?
x: The Kalachuris ruled from Tripuri near Jabalpur; Dhara was Paramara and Anhilwada Solanki.

s: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar in Delhi is a work of which dynasty?
x: The Iron Pillar is a Gupta work only moved to Delhi; it is not Anangapala's.

s: Who was the founder of the Chahamana (Chauhan) dynasty?
x: Vasudeva founded the Chahamanas, whose capital moved from Sakambhari to Ajmer.

s: Who was the founder of the Tomara dynasty that ruled from Dhillika (Delhi)?
x: The Tomaras of Dhillika (Delhi) were founded by Anangapala.

s: Who founded the Paramara dynasty?
x: Upendra (Krishnaraja) founded the Paramaras; Vasudeva founded the Chauhans, Nannuka the Chandelas and Mularaja I the Solankis.

s: Who was the last Paramara ruler, killed in 1305 by Alauddin's forces?
x: Mahalakadeva was the last Paramara, killed in 1305.

s: What do Muslims call the Bhojshala at Dhar, linked to Paramara Bhoja?
x: Muslims call Bhojshala the Kamal Maula Mosque; it became a mosque in the 14th century.

s: Which inscription gives the Paramara genealogy and praises Bhoja?
x: The Udaipur Prashasti gives the Paramara genealogy and praises Bhoja.

s: In which year was the ASI survey of Bhojshala at Dhar ordered?
x: The ASI survey was ordered in 2024; 2003 is the year of the ASI arrangement for worship on separate days.

s: To which deity is the unfinished Bhojeshwar temple at Bhojpur, beside Bhoja's man-made lake, dedicated?
x: The Bhojpur (Bhojeshwar) temple in Raisen district is a Shiva temple with a huge linga.

s: What does Bhoja's Saraswati-Kanthabharana deal with?
x: Saraswati-Kanthabharana is on poetics and grammar; Samarangana Sutradhara is on architecture.

s: Who is the author of Samarangana Sutradhara, a treatise on architecture?
x: Samarangana Sutradhara, on architecture and machines, was written by the Paramara king Bhoja.

s: The Bhojshala at Dhar, built by Paramara Bhoja, was a temple of which deity?
x: Bhojshala was a centre of Sanskrit learning with a temple of Saraswati (Vagdevi).

s: Which High Court declared the Bhojshala at Dhar a Hindu temple on the basis of ASI findings in May 2026?
x: In May 2026 the Madhya Pradesh High Court declared Bhojshala a Hindu temple on ASI findings.

s: Over whom did Rana Kumbha win the victory that the Vijaya Stambha at Chittor commemorates?
x: Rana Kumbha built the Vijaya Stambha at Chittor to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Khalji of Malwa.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kumbhalgarh fort was built by Rana Kumbha.
2. The Kirti Stambha at Chittor was built by the Jain merchant Jijaji in the 12th century.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Rana Kumbha built Kumbhalgarh, and the Kirti Stambha was built by the Jain merchant Jijaji.

s: What is the name of the work on music written by Rana Kumbha?
x: Rana Kumbha wrote Sangeet Raj (Sangeet Mimansa) on music.

s: Who wrote Navasahasanka Charita?
x: Navasahasanka Charita is by Padmagupta; Bhoja wrote Samarangana Sutradhara and Dalpati Vijay Khuman Raso.

s: Who wrote Bisaldeva Raso?
x: Bisaldeva Raso, on Vigraharaja IV, was written by Narapati (Nalha); Jagnik wrote Alha Khand.

s: Who wrote the play Lalita Vigraharaja?
x: Somadeva wrote Lalita Vigraharaja on Vigraharaja IV.

s: Who wrote Kirtikaumudi, about the Vaghela minister Vastupala?
x: Someshvara wrote Kirtikaumudi on Vastupala.

s: Who wrote Khuman Raso of Mewar?
x: Khuman Raso is by Dalpati Vijay, not Karnidan; Dungar Singh wrote Shatrusal Raso.

s: Navasahasanka Charita of Padmagupta is a biography of which Paramara ruler?
x: Padmagupta (Parimala), court poet of the Paramaras, wrote Navasahasanka Charita about Sindhuraja, whose title was Navasahasanka.

s: Which architectural feature is often associated with the Maru-Gurjara sub-style?
x: The Maru-Gurjara style, associated with the Solanki tradition of Gujarat and Rajasthan, often includes a Kirti-torana.

s: Which one of the following descriptions correctly refers to the Latina or Rekha-prasada type of Nagara temple tower?
o: A pyramidal tower with multiple terraces
x: Latina, also called Rekha-prasada, is characterised by a single curvilinear tower. Phamsana has a sloping, stepped roof, while Valabhi is barrel-vaulted.

s: With which dynasty is the Maru-Gurjara style of the 11th-13th centuries associated?
x: Maru-Gurjara is a Solanki-associated Nagara sub-style of Gujarat and Rajasthan, fusing Maha-Maru and Maha-Gurjara traditions.

s: In R. S. Sharma's model of 'Indian feudalism', what does vishti mean?
x: Sharma's model includes sub-infeudation and vishti (forced labour), with closed village economies.

s: Which of the following statements regarding women and Rajput customs is correct?
o: Sati was entirely unknown in Rajput society
Rani Padmini performed naval warfare against Alauddin Khalji
Jauhar meant the ritual coronation of a queen after victory
Jauhar involved self-immolation to avoid capture
x: Jauhar was self-immolation by women to avoid capture. Rani Padmini of Chittor is cited as an example in the conflict with Alauddin Khalji; sati was also practised.

s: On which of the following did Rajput warfare generally place emphasis?
x: Rajput warfare emphasised direct combat and personal valour, with chivalry and clan honour receiving great importance.

s: Against whom did the jauhar of Rani Padmini of Chittor take place?
x: Rani Padmini's jauhar at Chittor is linked to Alauddin Khalji's attack.

s:
Consider the following statements about Rajput society:
1. Land grants carried revenue, judicial and police rights.
2. Rajput warfare relied mainly on guerrilla tactics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Land grants carried revenue, judicial and police rights; Rajput warfare was direct face-to-face combat, not guerrilla war.

s: Rihla, the travel account of Ibn Battuta, was written in which language?
x: Ibn Battuta’s travel account, Rihla, was written in Arabic.

s:
Arrange the following foreign visitors in the order of their arrival in India:
1. Ibn Battuta
2. Manucci
3. Al-Biruni
4. Tavernier
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Al-Biruni (11th c.) came first, then Ibn Battuta (14th c.), Tavernier and Manucci (17th c.).

s: Which traveller is associated with observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets in the Delhi Sultanate?
x: Ibn Battuta’s account of Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s reign contains observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets.

s: Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara in 1443–44 as an envoy sent by which ruler?
x: Abdur Razzaq was a Persian envoy of Shah Rukh and visited the court of Deva Raya II in 1443–44.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ibn Battuta — Morocco — Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Abdur Razzaq — Portugal — Deva Raya II
x: Ibn Battuta was from Morocco and visited the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Marco Polo was from Venice, Abdur Razzaq from Persia and Duarte Barbosa from Portugal.

s: Afanasy Nikitin, a horse merchant who visited India during the reign of Virupaksha Raya II, belonged to which country?
x: Afanasy Nikitin was a Russian horse merchant from Tver on the Volga. He visited the Bahmani kingdom under Muhammad Shah III (from 1469).

s: During whose reign did Marco Polo visit Andhra?
x: Marco Polo came in Rudramadevi's reign; Nicolo Conti came under Devaraya I.

s: What did Tavernier, the 17th-century traveller, visit Andhra to see?
x: Tavernier, a 17th-century French jeweller, visited the Golconda-Andhra diamond mines for trade.

s: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire is based principally on the accounts of which group?
o: Barbosa, Seydi Ali Reis and Mahmud Wali Balkhi
Marco Polo, Ibn Battuta and Tavernier
x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire draws chiefly on the accounts of Paes, Nuniz and Abdur Razzaq.

s: During whose reign did Nicolo Conti visit Vijayanagara around 1420?
x: Nicolo Conti of Venice came c. 1420 under Deva Raya I; Abdur Razzaq came under Deva Raya II.

s: Which country did Duarte Barbosa, who wrote on Vijayanagara, come from?
x: Duarte Barbosa was Portuguese.

s: Itsing, who saw Indian students memorising Nagarjuna's Suhrllekha, was a pilgrim from which country?
x: Itsing was a Chinese pilgrim.

s: At which port did the Venetian traveller Marco Polo land in Andhra in 1292?
x: Marco Polo visited Motupalli in 1292 during Rudramadevi's reign.

s:
Consider the following statements about Marco Polo:
1. He came from Venice.
2. His account is the first foreign reference to a female ruler in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Marco Polo was a Venetian; his Travels refer to Rudramadevi, the first foreign reference to a female ruler in India.

s: Which Russian traveller visited the Bahmani kingdom during the reign of Muhammad Shah III?
x: Afanasy Nikitin of Tver, Russia, a horse merchant, visited the Bahmani kingdom under Muhammad Shah III.

s: Which post did Muhammad bin Tughlaq give Ibn Battuta?
x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta the qazi of Delhi and later sent him as envoy to China.

s: To which country was Ibn Battuta sent as envoy by Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
x: Ibn Battuta was sent as Muhammad bin Tughlaq's envoy to China.

s: To which country did Tavernier, the 17th-century jeweller who described the Golconda diamonds, belong?
x: Jean-Baptiste Tavernier was a French jeweller who visited Golconda under Abdullah Qutb Shah.

s: Who among the following wrote Storia do Mogor?
x: Niccolao Manucci, a Venetian artilleryman under Dara Shikoh, wrote Storia do Mogor.

s: During whose reign did the Portuguese traveller Domingo Paes visit Vijayanagara around 1520?
x: Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveller from Goa, visited Vijayanagara around 1520 in Krishnadeva Raya's reign.

s: Which Portuguese traveller compared the city of Vijayanagara to Rome in size?
x: Domingo Paes wrote that the city seemed to him as large as Rome.

s: Which pair is NOT correctly matched?
x: Kitab-ul-Hind was written by Al-Biruni, not Firdausi. The other three source-author pairs are correctly matched.

s: To whom did Minhaj-us-Siraj dedicate his Tabaqat-i-Nasiri?
x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud; Hasan Nizami's Taj-ul-Maasir was patronised by Aibak.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi — Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi
x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad. Badauni’s own historical work was Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the periods covered by Persian chronicles?
o: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri covers a period earlier than Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.
Tabaqat-i-Akbari covers the period up to Akbar's reign.
Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi covers a period earlier than Taj-ul-Maasir.
x: The order of periods covered is Taj-ul-Maasir, Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, Tabaqat-i-Akbari, so Taj-ul-Maasir is earlier than Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

s: Who wrote Fawaid-ul-Fawad?
x: Fawaid-ul-Fawad is by Amir Hasan Sijzi; Barani wrote Fatwa-i-Jahandari and Hasan Nizami Taj-ul-Masir.

s: Fatawa-i-Jahandari is primarily a work on which subject?
o: The postal system of the Delhi Sultanate
x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari, written by Ziauddin Barani, deals with political theory and kingship.

s: Who wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur's 1310 invasion of Warangal?
x: Amir Khusrau, court poet of Alauddin Khalji, wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied the 1310 expedition.

s: Which of the following source–author pairs is correctly matched?
x: Futuh-us-Salatin was written by Isami; Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is by Ziauddin Barani and Khazain-ul-Futuh by Amir Khusrau.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Firishta — Muhammad Qasim Firishta — Deccan history
Hadikat-us-Salatin — Ali bin Tahir Bustani — Qutb Shahis
Kumara Ramana Charitam — Kannada — South India after the fall of Warangal
x: Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan and deals with Aurangzeb’s conquest of Golconda. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.

s: To whom was Tarikh-i-Firishta (Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi) dedicated?
x: Firishta, born at Astarabad in 1552, dedicated his work to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur, not to a Qutb Shahi ruler.

s: Who wrote Tabaqat-i-Akbari?
x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari is by Nizamuddin Ahmad; Badauni wrote Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.

s: Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin around 1350 at which court?
x: Abdul Malik Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin at the Bahmani court c. 1350.

s: Who wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, on the Sayyid Sultan Mubarak Shah?
x: Yahya bin Ahmad Sarhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi.

s: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri of Minhaj-us-Siraj comprises how many volumes?
x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri has 23 volumes and was translated into English by H.G. Raverty.

s: Which work gives the earliest reference to the use of the magnetic compass in the Indian seas?
x: Sadiduddin Muhammad Aufi's Jawami-ul-Hikayat has the earliest reference to the magnetic compass in the Indian seas.

s: Which source calls Telangana 'Tilang'?
x: Firishta's Tarikh-i-Firishta (Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi), dedicated to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur, calls Telangana 'Tilang'.

s: Who was the patron of Hasan Nizami, author of Taj-ul-Maasir?
x: Taj-ul-Maasir of Hasan Nizami covers the early Sultanate; its patron was Aibak.

s: Besides Ziauddin Barani, who wrote a work titled Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi?
x: Both Barani and Shams-i-Siraj Afif wrote works called Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

s: Who is the author of Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh?
x: Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh was written by Badauni; Tabaqat-i-Akbari is by Nizamuddin Ahmad.

s: Who translated Minhaj-us-Siraj's Tabaqat-i-Nasiri into English?
x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (23 volumes) was translated into English by H.G. Raverty.

s: Who wrote Muntakhab-ul-Lubab, which describes Aurangzeb's conquest of Golconda?
x: Muntakhab-ul-Lubab is by Khafi Khan; it covers Aurangzeb's conquest of Golconda.

s: According to Al-Biruni’s account, which of the following was observed on Kartika Amavasya?
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kampana
The coronation of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
The annual court of the Qutb Shahis
x: Al-Biruni recorded the celebration of Diwali on Kartika Amavasya.

s: In which language did Al-Biruni, who learned Sanskrit, write his account of India?
x: Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and wrote in Arabic on Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste.

s: Al-Biruni, who came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni, was a native of which place?
x: Al-Biruni came from Khwarazm in Central Asia, in present Uzbekistan. Tangiers was Ibn Battuta's birthplace, Balkh was Mahmud Wali Balkhi's home, and Astarabad was Firishta's birthplace.

s: Madhura Vijayam provides information chiefly about which of the following?
o: Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule
The conquest of Golconda by Aurangzeb
The life of Pala king Ramapala
x: Madhura Vijayam, written by Gangadevi, describes Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule.

s: Sandhyakara Nandi's Ramacharitam tells the Ramayana together with the story of which Pala king?
x: Ramacharitam is a double-meaning poem on the Ramayana and the Pala king Ramapala.

s: Who wrote Hadikat-us-Salatin, a Persian chronicle of the Qutb Shahis?
x: Ali bin Tahir Bustani wrote Hadikat-us-Salatin; Zuberi wrote Basatin-us-Salatin.

s: How many tarangas (books) does Kalhana's Rajatarangini have?
x: Kalhana's Rajatarangini ("River of Kings"), the 12th-century history of Kashmir, has 8 tarangas.

s: Who is the author of Rajatarangini, the history of Kashmir?
x: Kalhana wrote Rajatarangini ('River of Kings'), a 12th-century history of Kashmir.

s: Who wrote Madhura Vijayam, describing Kampana's conquest of Madurai?
x: Madhura Vijayam was written by Gangadevi about Kampana's conquest of Madurai.

s: Madhura Vijayam of Gangadevi gives information about conditions in Madurai under the rule of which dynasty before Kampana's conquest?
x: Madhura Vijayam describes Kampana's conquest of Madurai and the conditions there under Tughlaq rule.

s: Who is the author of the modern work 'History of the Qutb Shahi Dynasty'?
x: H.K. Sherwani wrote History of the Qutb Shahi Dynasty.

s: Who founded the Golconda school of painting?
x: The Golconda school of painting was founded by Mir Hashimi.

s: The transition from trabeate to arcuate construction in Sultanate architecture is marked by the increasing use of what?
o: Wooden pillars and flat roofs only
Timber frames and corbelled balconies only
True arches, domes and lime mortar
x: Sultanate buildings demonstrate the shift from trabeate construction to arcuate construction through the use of true arches, domes and lime mortar.

s: In Qutb Shahi calligraphy, in which script were Quranic verses written?
x: Naskh was used for Quranic verses, including those in the Jami Masjid mihrab; Nastaliq was used for Persian texts.

s: In Qutb Shahi calligraphy, for what was the Nastaliq script used?
x: Nastaliq was used for Persian texts; Naskh was used for Quranic verses.

s: The Golconda manuscript 'Quliyat Quli' contains how many miniatures?
x: The Quliyat Quli manuscript has 14 miniatures.

s: The Palam Baoli inscription of 1276 praises which ruler in Sanskrit?
x: The Palam Baoli inscription, dated 1276, praises Balban in Sanskrit.

s: To which year does the Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda date Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's independence?
x: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda dates the independence of Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk to 1518.

s: What do Mahmud of Ghazni's Lahore dirhams contain that makes them especially significant as medieval sources?
o: An Arabic legend and its Sanskrit translation in Sharada script
A Telugu inscription and an Arabic translation
A Sanskrit legend and its Persian translation in Devanagari script
Only a Persian inscription in Nastaliq script
x: The Lahore dirhams of Mahmud of Ghazni carry an Arabic legend along with a Sanskrit translation written in Sharada script.

s: Unlike Mahmud's bilingual coins, in what language were the legends on the coins of Iltutmish?
x: Iltutmish's silver tanka and copper jital were purely Arabic; Mahmud's Lahore dirhams were Arabic plus Sanskrit.

s: Who issued the Vilasa copper plate (c. 1330)?
x: The Vilasa copper plate belongs to Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka; the Kaluvacheru record belongs to Anitalli.

s: In which language was Babur's memoir Tuzuk-i-Baburi written?
x: The Baburnama was written in Turki.

s: Who wrote the Humayun-nama?
x: Humayun-nama was written by Gulbadan Begum, Babur's daughter, at Akbar's request.

s: The Ain-i-Akbari forms which volume of the Akbarnama?
x: The Ain-i-Akbari is the third volume of Abul Fazl's Akbarnama, dealing with administration and revenue.

s: At whose request did Gulbadan Begum write the Humayun-nama?
x: She wrote it at Akbar's request.

s: Who is the author of Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri?
x: Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is Jahangir's autobiography.

s: Foreign travellers' accounts of medieval India should generally be used by historians in which manner?
o: They should replace inscriptions and archaeological evidence.
They should be ignored because they were written outside India.
They should be accepted as accurate in every detail.
They should supplement Indian texts and be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeology.
x: Foreign accounts supplement Indian textual evidence, but their statements must be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeological evidence.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes Ziauddin Barani?
o: He wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and theorised kingship.
He was a Persian ambassador to Vijayanagara and described its markets.
He founded the Golconda school of painting.
He composed the royal memoirs of Jahangir.
x: Ziauddin Barani wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and also theorised about kingship. The other descriptions belong to different figures or traditions.

s: Firishta's story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal is, by modern historians:
x: Modern historians reject Firishta's story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal, showing the need to evaluate chronicles critically.

s: According to Telugu sources such as Pratapa Charitra, Warangal was invaded how many times?
x: Telugu sources (Pratapa Charitra, Vilasa, Kaluvacheru) record eight invasions; Muslim sources record five.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about biases in medieval chronicles?
o: Court histories tend to glorify the patron.
Barani wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint.
Amir Khusrau was court poet of Alauddin Khalji.
Firishta's story of Deva Raya kidnapping Nehal is accepted by modern historians.
x: Modern historians reject Firishta's story of Deva Raya kidnapping Nehal.

s: In what capacity did Balban serve during the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud?
x: Balban was Nasiruddin Mahmud's principal minister, or naib, and leader of the Forty. He was briefly displaced by Imaduddin Raihan before returning to power.

s: Which sequence correctly describes Balban's early rise?
o: Slave of Iltutmish → water-carrier → member of the Forty → Amir-i-Shikar
Water-carrier → slave of Aibak → Amir-i-Akhur → member of the Forty
Member of the Forty → slave of Iltutmish → water-carrier → governor of Bhatinda
x: Balban was captured by the Mongols, bought by Iltutmish, rose from water-carrier to the Forty, and was made Amir-i-Shikar by Razia.

s: Which title did Balban hold as naib of Nasiruddin Mahmud?
x: Balban, principal minister and leader of the Forty, bore the title Ulugh Khan.

s: Who briefly displaced Balban from power during Nasiruddin Mahmud's reign?
x: Imaduddin Raihan briefly displaced Balban, who then returned to power.

s: What was Balban's original name?
x: Balban was born c. 1205 as Bahauddin; captured by the Mongols, he was bought by Iltutmish.

s: How did Balban break the power of the Forty?
x: Balban broke the Forty's power by promoting junior Turks; he did not strengthen the Forty.

s: By which title did Balban describe the Sultan?
x: Balban held the Sultan to be Zil-i-Ilahi (shadow of God) and required sijda and paibos.

s: In Balban's court, what did 'paibos' mean?
x: Paibos was kissing the feet; sijda was prostration and zil-i-ilahi meant shadow of God.

s: Which of the following is wrongly matched about Balban's court?
x: Sijda meant prostration; kissing the feet was paibos.

s: From which finance department did Balban separate the military department Diwan-i-Arz?
x: Balban's Diwan-i-Arz was separated from the Diwan-i-Wizarat, the finance department.

s: On what did Balban's defence against the Mongols mainly rely?
o: Outposts and forts on the frontier
x: Balban built outposts and forts against the Mongols.

s: What was the military department reorganised by Balban known as?
x: Balban reorganised the army and created the military department Diwan-i-Arz. He also built outposts and forts against the Mongols.

s: From where to where did Iltutmish shift the capital of the Sultanate?
x: Iltutmish moved the capital from Lahore (Aibak's capital) to Delhi.

s: Iltutmish refused shelter to which Khwarazmian prince, helping keep Chengiz Khan out of India?
x: Iltutmish refused shelter to Jalaluddin Mangbarni of Khwarazm, which helped keep Chengiz Khan out of India.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to Iltutmish is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Turkan-i-Chahalgani – Body of Persian revenue clerks
Iqta – Revenue assignment in place of cash salary
Mansur (1229) – Investiture from the Abbasid Caliph
x: The Turkan-i-Chahalgani (the Forty) was the Turkish military elite, not a body of Persian revenue clerks.

s: To whom was the Qutb Minar dedicated?
x: The Qutb Minar, begun by Aibak and completed by Iltutmish, is dedicated to the Sufi saint Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.

s: Which monument led to Iltutmish being called the ‘Father of tomb building’?
x: Iltutmish built the Sultan Ghari tomb and is consequently called the Father of tomb building. He also completed the Qutb Minar.

s: Which coins did Iltutmish introduce as regular Arabic coinage?
x: Iltutmish brought in the silver tanka and the copper jital, a regular, purely Arabic coinage.

s: In which year did Iltutmish receive investiture ('mansur') from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad?
x: In 1229 Iltutmish received the first Caliphal investiture from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad.

s: In which year did Iltutmish defeat his rival Tajuddin Yildiz at Tarain?
x: Yildiz was defeated at Tarain in 1216; 1192 was the second battle of Tarain under Ghori.

s: Who were the Turkan-i-Chahalgani or 'the Forty' created by Iltutmish?
x: The Forty (Chalisa) were a Turkish military elite, not Persian revenue clerks.

s: Under Iltutmish, what were the officers who held revenue assignments instead of cash salaries called?
x: Iqtas were revenue assignments given to officers called muqtis in place of cash salaries.

s: Which rival of Iltutmish fought him for Lahore?
x: Iltutmish's rivals were Yildiz and Nasiruddin Qabacha, who fought for Lahore.

s: Who completed the Qutb Minar, begun by Qutbuddin Aibak?
x: Aibak began the Qutb Minar, but it was completed by Iltutmish.

s: What does Qutbuddin Aibak's title 'Lakh Bakhsh' mean?
x: Lakh Bakhsh means 'giver of lakhs'; 'shadow of God' (Zil-i-Ilahi) is Balban's idea of the Sultan.

s: Which office did Qutbuddin Aibak hold before becoming a general?
x: Aibak rose to the position of Amir-i-Akhur, or Master of Stables, and subsequently became a general.

s: Whose slave was Qutbuddin Aibak?
x: Aibak, sold first to the Qazi of Nishapur, became the slave of Muhammad Ghori (asked in APPSC Group 1, 2004).

s: What was the capital of Qutbuddin Aibak?
x: Aibak ruled from Lahore; Iltutmish later moved the capital to Delhi.

s: Which was the first mosque in Delhi, begun by Qutbuddin Aibak?
x: Aibak began the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, the first mosque in Delhi; Adhai Din ka Jhonpra is at Ajmer.

s: Where is the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra, begun by Qutbuddin Aibak, located?
x: Aibak began the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer, along with the Qutb Minar and Quwwat-ul-Islam in Delhi.

s: While playing which game did Qutbuddin Aibak die in 1210?
x: Aibak died at Lahore in 1210 after falling from his horse while playing chaugan (polo), a game brought to India by the Turks.

s: Where was Qutbuddin Aibak buried?
x: Aibak died at Lahore, his capital, in 1210 and was buried near Anarkali Bazaar there.

s: Which of the following was a distinctive feature of Razia Sultan's rule?
o: She accepted the authority of Bahram Shah throughout her reign.
She maintained purdah and never appeared before the army.
She discarded purdah, wore male attire and led the army.
She ruled only through Balban as her regent.
x: Razia discarded purdah, wore male attire and personally led the army. Her conduct challenged the expectations of the Turkish nobles.

s: The Turkish nobles opposed Razia primarily because she favoured whom?
x: The Turkish nobles resented Razia's favour towards Yaqut, an Abyssinian. Their opposition contributed to the revolt led by Altuniya.

s: Altuniya, who revolted against Razia in 1240, was the governor of which place?
x: Altuniya was governor of Bhatinda (Sirhind); his revolt led to Yaqut's death and Razia's imprisonment.

s:
Consider the following statements about Razia Sultan:
1. She was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
2. She married Altuniya and was killed after marching on Delhi.
3. She made Balban Diwan-i-Arz.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Razia was the only woman Sultan and married Altuniya before her defeat in 1240; she made Balban Amir-i-Shikar, not Diwan-i-Arz.

s: What was the nationality of Yaqut, Razia's favourite who was resented by the Turkish nobles?
x: Yaqut was an Abyssinian; the Turkish nobles resented Razia's favour to him.

s: Which dynasty succeeded the Mamluks on the throne of Delhi in 1290?
x: The Mamluk dynasty (1206–1290) was followed by the Khaljis (1290–1320), then the Tughlaqs, Sayyids and Lodis.

s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the Mamluk dynasty?
x: Jalaluddin Khalji belonged to the Khalji dynasty. Alauddin Masud, Nasiruddin Mahmud and Ruknuddin Firuz were rulers of the Mamluk dynasty.

s: Which Mamluk ruler immediately preceded Balban?
x: Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-66) was followed by Balban (1266-86).

s: What does the term 'Mamluk' literally refer to?
x: Mamluk is an Arabic term meaning ‘owned’. In this context it denotes a military slave, distinct from a domestic slave.

s: During which period did the Mamluk dynasty rule from Delhi?
x: The Mamluk or Slave dynasty ruled from 1206 to 1290, when the Khaljis took over.

s: Who founded the Second Ilbari line of the Mamluk dynasty?
x: Balban founded the Second Ilbari line (1266-1290); Iltutmish founded the First Ilbari line and Aibak the Qutbi line.

s:
Consider the following statements about the lines of the Mamluk dynasty:
1. The Qutbi line was founded by Qutbuddin Aibak.
2. The First Ilbari line was founded by Balban.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Aibak founded the Qutbi line; the First Ilbari line was founded by Iltutmish, while Balban founded the Second Ilbari line.

s: Who succeeded Iltutmish immediately on the throne of Delhi in 1236?
x: Iltutmish was followed by Ruknuddin Firuz (1236) and then Razia (1236-40).

s:
Arrange the following dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate in chronological order:
1. Sayyid
2. Khalji
3. Lodi
4. Tughlaq
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Mamluk (1206) → Khalji (1290) → Tughlaq (1320) → Sayyid (1414) → Lodi (1451-1526).

s: The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is named after which Sultan?
x: The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is named after Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-66), whose naib was Balban.

s: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at which place in 1290?
x: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290, thereby ending Mamluk rule and beginning the Khalji dynasty.

s: Which sequence correctly describes the end of Mamluk rule?
o: Balban → Kaiqubad → Kaimurs → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji
Kaiqubad → Balban → Kaimurs → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji
Balban → Kaimurs → Kaiqubad → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji
Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji → Balban → Kaiqubad → Kaimurs
x: Balban died in 1286 and was followed by his grandson Kaiqubad, who was murdered. The infant Kaimurs succeeded him briefly before Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji ended Mamluk rule in 1290.

s: Who was the grandson of Balban who succeeded him and was later murdered?
x: Kaiqubad, Balban's grandson, was murdered and his body thrown into the Yamuna; infant Kaimurs followed.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Mamluk dynasty?
x: The infant Kaimurs was the last Mamluk before Jalaluddin Khalji crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290.

s: Against which kingdom was Malik Kafur's first southern campaign (1307-08)?
x: The order was Devagiri (1307-08), Warangal (1309-10), Dwarasamudra (1310-11) and Madurai (1311).

s: Which of the following pairs on Kakatiya–Delhi relations is correctly matched?
o: 1309–10 – Kakatiya help to Delhi against the Pandyas
1311 – Treaty between Malik Kafur and the Kakatiyas
1303 – Kakatiya defeat of a Delhi army at Upparapalli
1316 – Start of Kakatiya tribute to Delhi
x: The Kakatiyas defeated a Delhi army at Upparapalli in 1303; the treaty was 1309–10, help against the Pandyas 1311, and tribute stopped after 1316.

s: Which Hoysala ruler of Dwarasamudra did Malik Kafur campaign against in 1310-11?
x: The Hoysala ruler Vira Ballala III of Dwarasamudra submitted in 1310-11.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Koh-i-Noor and Malik Kafur:
1. A later popular tradition says Kafur obtained it from Prataparudra at Warangal.
2. A contemporary record confirms Kafur obtained it at Warangal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Koh-i-Noor story is only a later popular tradition; there is no contemporary record of it.

s: After which year did Kakatiya tribute to Delhi under the 1309-10 treaty stop?
x: After the 1309-10 treaty and help against the Pandyas in 1311, the Kakatiya tribute stopped after 1316.

s: Whose troops aided Malik Kafur in his 1311 campaign against Madurai?
x: Under the 1309-10 treaty, Kakatiya troops aided Kafur against the Pandyas of Madurai in 1311.

s: According to Telugu sources, how many times was Warangal invaded by the Delhi Sultanate?
x: Telugu sources count 8 invasions of Warangal; Muslim sources count 5.

s: Why was Malik Kafur called 'Hazar Dinari'?
o: He was bought for a thousand dinars
He was paid a thousand dinars a day
He minted a thousand gold coins
x: Malik Kafur, taken by Nusrat Khan in the Gujarat campaign, was called Hazar Dinari because he was bought for a thousand dinars.

s: Which Kakatiya ruler made a treaty with Malik Kafur in 1309-10 and agreed to pay annual tribute?
x: In 1309-10 Malik Kafur besieged Warangal; the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra II made a treaty and agreed to pay annual tribute.

s:
Arrange the following campaigns of Malik Kafur in chronological order:
1. Dwarasamudra
2. Devagiri
3. Madurai
4. Warangal
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Kafur attacked Devagiri (1307-08), Warangal (1309-10), Dwarasamudra (1310-11) and Madurai (1311), in that order.

s: Which Yadava ruler of Devagiri agreed to pay tribute after Malik Kafur's campaign of 1307-08?
x: Ramachandra of Devagiri agreed to pay tribute in 1307-08.

s: Under which Sultan was the south annexed to the Delhi Sultanate, after Malik Kafur's tribute-seeking campaigns?
x: Kafur's campaigns sought tribute; annexation came only under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

s: Khusrau Khan's campaign against Warangal during the reign of Mubarak Shah is regarded as which invasion of the Kakatiya kingdom?
x: Khusrau Khan subdued Warangal again in 1318, which is identified as the third invasion.

s: The first attack on Warangal in 1303 ended in failure at Upparapalli. Which pair of Kakatiya commanders defeated Malik Fakhruddin Juna there?
o: Hamir Deva and Rana Ratan Singh
x: Potuganti Maili and Recherla Venna defeated Malik Fakhruddin Juna at Upparapalli during the failed 1303 attack on Warangal.

s: Who accompanied Malik Kafur on his second expedition against Warangal (1309-10)?
x: Malik Kafur and Khwaja Haji besieged Warangal, won Prataparudra's submission and sent loot to Delhi on 1,000 camels.

s: How does Amir Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh describe the Warangal fort?
o: a single mud wall with no moat
x: Khazain-ul-Futuh describes Warangal's double-walled fort, its moat and the diamond mines; Khusrau accompanied the 1310 campaign.

s: Which of the following Deccan campaign–ruler/outcome pairs is correctly matched?
x: Devagiri was ruled by Ramachandra. Warangal was under Prataparudra II, Dwarasamudra under Vira Ballala III, and the Pandya kingdom of Madurai was sacked.

s: Which one of the following statements about Malik Kafur is correct?
o: He was a eunuch, later rose to Malik Naib, and participated in the Deccan campaigns.
He was a court historian who wrote Futuh-us-Salatin.
He was a hereditary Rajput commander who became governor of Kara.
He was the Kakatiya ruler who negotiated tribute with Delhi.
x: Malik Kafur was a eunuch purchased during the Gujarat campaign, later rose to Malik Naib and led important Deccan campaigns.

s: Against whom was Malik Kafur's 1310-11 campaign?
x: In 1310-11 Kafur marched against the Hoysalas of Dwarasamudra under Vira Ballala III.

s: To which rank did Malik Kafur, called 'Hazar Dinari', rise?
x: Kafur, a eunuch bought for 1,000 dinars, rose to be Malik Naib (deputy).

s: Where did Alauddin Khalji take shelter when the Mongols besieged Delhi?
x: Alauddin sheltered in Siri during the siege; Zafar Khan was killed at Kili.

s: What did repeated Mongol invasions during Alauddin Khalji's reign lead him to maintain?
o: a feudal levy of Rajput chiefs
x: The Mongol threat led Alauddin to keep a large standing army, with military reforms and revenue and market reforms to pay for it.

s: Which one of the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's defence against the Mongols is NOT correct?
o: He abandoned the north-western frontier and concentrated all forces in the Deccan.
He maintained a large standing army.
He built Siri as a new capital.
He repaired old forts and constructed new ones on the north-western frontier.
x: Alauddin did not abandon the north-western frontier. He repaired and built forts, maintained a large standing army, established Siri and appointed Ghazi Malik as governor of Punjab.

s: Who led the Mongols in the Battle of Kili (1299)?
x: Qutlugh Khwaja led the Mongols at Kili in 1299; Targhi besieged Delhi in 1303.

s: Who led the Mongol siege of Delhi in 1303?
x: Targhi besieged Delhi in 1303, and Alauddin sheltered in Siri fort.

s: Ghazi Malik is said to have chased away the Mongols how many times?
x: By 1320 Ghazi Malik had chased the Mongols 29 times.

s: In which year did Chengiz Khan reach the Indus, chasing Jalaluddin Mangbarni?
x: Chengiz Khan reached the Indus in 1221 under Iltutmish; this was the first Mongol threat.

s: Who invaded Delhi in 1398, during the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq?
x: Timur invaded Delhi in 1398 under Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq.

s: Alauddin Khalji defeated the Mongols at which of the following places in 1298, 1299, 1305 and 1306 respectively?
x: The Mongol defeats associated with the four years were Jalandhar in 1298, Kili in 1299, Amroha in 1305 and Ravi in 1306.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's defence against the Mongols:
1. After 1306 the Ravi became the boundary between the Sultanate and the Mongols.
2. He repaired the forts on the north-western frontier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: after the Mongol defeat of 1306 the Ravi became the boundary river, and the frontier forts were repaired.

s: Which Vaghela ruler of Gujarat was defeated by Alauddin Khalji's forces?
x: Gujarat's Rai Karan (Karnadeva II Vaghela) was defeated; Ratan Singh was of Chittor and Mahlak Deva of Malwa.

s: Which pair of officials led Alauddin Khalji's Gujarat campaign of 1299?
o: Khwaja Haji and Malik Fakhruddin Juna
x: Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan commanded the Gujarat campaign of 1299. Rai Karan, also known as Karnadeva II, was defeated, and Queen Kamala Devi was captured.

s: What did Alauddin Khalji rename Chittor as?
x: After the conquest of Chittor in 1303, Alauddin Khalji renamed it Khizrabad after his son Prince Khizr Khan.

s: Under Alauddin Khalji's southern policy, how were conquered rulers generally treated?
o: allowed to keep their thrones on paying tribute
annexed and their kingdoms made provinces
x: In the south rulers kept their thrones and paid tribute, whereas northern kingdoms were generally annexed.

s: In which year did Alauddin Khalji conquer Malwa?
x: Malwa fell in 1305, after Gujarat (1299), Ranthambhor (1301) and Chittor (1303).

s: In which year did Alauddin Khalji conquer Gujarat?
x: Gujarat was conquered in 1299 (APPSC 2023 key), not 1297.

s: Which Chauhan ruler of Ranthambore was defeated by Alauddin Khalji in 1301?
x: Hammir Deva Chauhan, who sheltered the New Mussalmans, was defeated at Ranthambore in 1301.

s: Which ruler of Malwa was defeated by Alauddin's general Ain-ul-Mulk in 1305?
x: Ain-ul-Mulk conquered Malwa from Mahlak Deva in 1305.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Alauddin Khalji's conquests?
o: Nusrat Khan was killed at Ranthambore
Chittor was taken from Rana Ratan Singh in 1303
Zafar Khan was killed at Ranthambore
x: Nusrat Khan was killed at Ranthambore; Zafar Khan was killed at the Battle of Kili (1299).

s: Which Vaghela queen of Gujarat was captured during Alauddin Khalji's Gujarat campaign of 1299?
x: In the 1299 Gujarat campaign queen Kamala Devi of Rai Karan was captured.

s: Which ruler of Siwana was defeated during Alauddin Khalji's campaigns in Rajputana (c. 1308-11)?
x: Shital Deva of Siwana was defeated; Rajputana was completed by c. 1311.

s: What was the significance of Alauddin Khalji's raid on Devagiri in the history of the Delhi Sultanate?
o: The first expedition of the Tughlaqs into the south
The first Kakatiya invasion of Delhi
The first Turkish invasion of southern India
The first Mongol invasion of the Deccan
x: Alauddin Khalji's Devagiri raid of 1294–96 is described as the first Turkish invasion of the south.

s: Who was the ruler of Ranthambhore defeated by Alauddin Khalji in 1301?
x: Hammir Deva ruled Ranthambhore (1301); Rai Karan was of Gujarat, Ratan Singh of Chittor and Mahlak Deva of Malwa.

s: Which of the following conquest–ruler pairs is wrongly matched?
x: Malwa's ruler was Mahlak Deva; Hammir Deva ruled Ranthambhore.

s:
Arrange the following conquests of Alauddin Khalji in chronological order:
1. Malwa
2. Gujarat
3. Chittor
4. Ranthambhore
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Gujarat fell in 1299, Ranthambhore in 1301, Chittor in 1303 and Malwa in 1305.

s: What does Alauddin Khalji's title 'Sikandar-i-Sani' mean?
x: Sikandar-i-Sani means the second Alexander; Alauddin wished to be a world conqueror like Alexander.

s: By what name was Alauddin Khalji known before becoming Sultan?
x: Alauddin Khalji's earlier name was Ali Gurshasp.

s: Under Jalaluddin Khalji, Alauddin was Amir-i-Tuzuk. What does this post mean?
x: Amir-i-Tuzuk was the master of ceremonies; the Ariz-i-Mumalik was the army minister.

s: On whose advice did Alauddin Khalji drop his plans of world conquest and a new religion?
x: Kotwal of Delhi Ala-ul-Mulk, Barani's uncle, advised him to drop both plans.

s: Alauddin Khalji told Qazi Mughisuddin of which place that he acted in the interest of the state?
x: Barani records Alauddin's talk with Qazi Mughisuddin of Bayana.

s: What were the state laws made by the ruler, distinguished by Barani from the Shariat, called?
x: Barani separated Shariat from Zawabit, the state laws made by the ruler.

s: Under Jalaluddin Khalji, what did Alauddin's post of Ariz-i-Mumalik mean?
x: Ariz-i-Mumalik was the army minister, not minister of law; Amir-i-Tuzuk was master of ceremonies.

s: Who was the court poet of Alauddin Khalji?
x: Amir Khusrau was Alauddin's court poet.

s: In matters of state policy, by what did Alauddin Khalji declare he would be guided?
x: Alauddin refused the Ulema's guidance and declared his actions would be governed by the interests of the state.

s: Alauddin Khalji revived the harsh, centralised rule of which earlier Sultan, though without depending on religious sanction?
x: Alauddin revived Balban's harsh, centralised rule but, unlike Balban, did not depend on religious sanction.

s: Who persuaded Alauddin Khalji to abandon both his plans for world conquest and a new religion?
x: Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk talked Alauddin out of both the plan for world conquest and the proposal for a new religion.

s: Which title, meaning 'the Second Alexander', did Alauddin Khalji take?
x: Alauddin Khalji called himself Sikandar-i-Sani, the Second Alexander, and dreamt of world conquest.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Bahlol Lodi ruled from 1451 to 1489, not 1491. The other three reign periods are correctly matched.

s: During which period did the Sayyid Sultan Khizr Khan rule?
x: Khizr Khan (Sayyid) ruled 1414-1421; he is different from Alauddin's son Khizr Khan, set aside in 1316.

s: Which of the following pairs of Sultan and reign is correctly matched?
x: Jalaluddin ruled 1290-1296; Alauddin ruled to 1316, Muhammad bin Tughlaq from 1325, and Bahlol Lodi to 1489.

s: Which of the following events occurred immediately after the death of Alauddin Khalji in 1316?
o: Ghazi Malik founded the Tughlaq dynasty.
Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and enthroned the minor Shihabuddin Umar.
Khusrau Khan subdued Warangal for the first time.
x: After Alauddin's death in 1316, Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and placed the minor Shihabuddin Umar on the throne.

s: Ghazi Malik's victory over whom marked the end of Khalji rule?
x: Ghazi Malik's victory over Khusrau Khan ended Khalji rule.

s: Who murdered Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah?
x: Khusrau Khan (Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah) murdered Mubarak Shah, and was killed by Ghazi Malik in 1320.

s: Who was the last Khalji Sultan of Delhi?
x: Mubarak Shah was the last Khalji Sultan; Khusrau Khan was a usurper.

s: Who founded the Tughlaq dynasty in 1320?
x: Ghazi Malik killed Khusrau Khan in 1320 and founded the Tughlaq dynasty as Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.

s: Who wrote Padmavat, the work that narrates the story of Padmini?
x: Padmavat was written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. It presents the Padmini story, which some scholars regard as a legend.

s: In which language was Padmavat composed?
x: Malik Muhammad Jayasi composed Padmavat in Awadhi. Some descriptions place it within the broader Hindi literary tradition.

s: In which year was the Padmini story, linked with Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Chittor, recorded in Padmavat?
x: The Padmini narrative was recorded in Padmavat in 1540; some scholars treat it as legend.

s: In which year did Alauddin Khalji conquer Chittor?
x: Alauddin defeated Rana Ratan Singh at Chittor in 1303, after which Padmini and the Rajput women performed jauhar.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Padmini legend:
1. Padmavat was written about two centuries after the Chittor conquest.
2. Rani Padmini and the Rajput women performed jauhar at Chittor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Padmavat (1540) came about two centuries after 1303, and the story says Padmini and the Rajput women performed jauhar.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes Jalaluddin Khalji's policy towards rebels and Hindus?
o: He imposed severe punishments on every rebel without exception.
He adopted a benevolent attitude and was lenient towards rebels such as Malik Chhajju.
He adopted a policy of complete exclusion of Hindus from administration.
He transferred the capital to Ranthambore to control Hindu chiefs.
x: Jalaluddin Khalji was the first Sultan described as having a benevolent attitude towards Hindus, and he was lenient towards rebels including Malik Chhajju.

s: Where was Jalaluddin Khalji murdered by Alauddin?
x: Jalaluddin, who crowned himself at Kilokhari, was murdered at Kara by Alauddin in 1296.

s: What were the Mongols who converted and settled in the Sultanate under Jalaluddin Khalji called?
x: Settled converted Mongols were called New Mussalmans; Jalaluddin also married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of Chengiz Khan.

s: Which rebel was treated leniently by Jalaluddin Khalji?
x: Jalaluddin was lenient to rebels such as Malik Chhajju.

s: Jalaluddin Khalji married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of whom?
x: Jalaluddin married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of Chengiz Khan.

s: Alauddin Khalji's market regulations aimed at price fixation, guaranteed supply, controlled distribution and what else?
x: The regulations fixed prices, guaranteed supply, controlled distribution and ended monopolistic practices.

s: Which of the following was NOT an aim of Alauddin Khalji's market control?
x: The aims were fixed prices, sure supply, rationing and the end of monopolies; it was not meant to pay palace artisans less.

s: Under Alauddin Khalji, what did the Sarai Adl market deal in?
o: cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter and oil
x: Sarai Adl dealt in cloth and similar commodities; the Mandi handled food grains.

s: Under Alauddin Khalji, who was the superintendent of an individual market?
x: The Shahna-i-Mandi supervised each market; the system ran under the Diwan-i-Riyasat, who worked under the Naib-i-Riyasat.

s: Which officer was associated with the recovery of arrears from revenue officials?
x: The Diwan-i-Mustakhraj was established to recover arrears from revenue officials. The Diwan-i-Riyasat was concerned with market administration.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Shahna-i-Mandi supervised a market. Land-revenue arrears were recovered by the Diwan-i-Mustakhraj, whereas barids, munhiyans and slave boys helped monitor market compliance.

s: Under Alauddin Khalji, what did the Mandi market mainly deal in?
x: The Mandi was the grain market; Sarai Adl dealt in cloth and other goods.

s: Which department ran the whole market system of Alauddin Khalji?
x: The Diwan-i-Riyasat, under the Naib-i-Riyasat, ran the markets; Diwan-i-Mustakhraj recovered revenue arrears.

s: How many separate markets did Alauddin Khalji set up?
x: There were four markets: Mandi (grain), Sarai Adl (cloth etc.), one for horses, slaves and cattle, and one for miscellaneous goods.

s: Which post did Malik Kabool hold under Alauddin Khalji?
x: Malik Kabool was a Shahna-i-Mandi, superintendent of a market.

s: In Alauddin Khalji's market system, which goods were sold in the third market?
x: Alauddin's third market dealt in horses, slaves and cattle.

s: What were the secret spies who sent daily reports to Alauddin Khalji called?
x: Alauddin reorganised spies, the barids and munhiyan, who sent daily reports.

s: Which of the following is regarded as a major significance of Alauddin Khalji’s economic and revenue measures?
o: They made religious institutions solely responsible for land measurement.
They introduced paper currency and decentralised all revenue administration.
They introduced the first state-run price-control and rationing system in India and the first land measurement for revenue.
They abolished all forms of taxation and ended state supervision of markets.
x: Alauddin’s measures are regarded as the first state-run price-control and rationing system in India and the first land measurement system for revenue assessment.

s: At what share did Alauddin Khalji fix the state's demand of produce (kharaj)?
x: The state share was one-half (50%); he was also the first Sultan to measure land, using the biswa.

s: What was the headman's cess abolished by Alauddin Khalji called?
x: Alauddin abolished the kismat-i-khuti and brought khuts, muqaddams and chaudharis under taxation.

s: Under Alauddin Khalji, on what was Ghari levied?
x: Ghari was the house tax; Charai was the grazing tax and Kharaj 50% of yield.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding Alauddin Khalji's revenue measures?
o: The privileges of Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary were expanded to strengthen intermediaries.
His measures weakened the role of traditional intermediary tax collectors.
The traditional tax-collection privileges of Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary were abolished.
Revenue was collected more directly by weakening intermediary tax collectors.
x: Option A is incorrect: Alauddin Khalji abolished, not expanded, the privileges of the Khuts, Muqaddams and Chaudharis. This weakened the intermediaries and let the state collect revenue more directly.

s: On what basis was Alauddin Khalji the first Sultan to assess land revenue?
x: Alauddin was the first Sultan to measure land (masahat), with the biswa as the standard unit.

s: What was the standard unit of land measurement under Alauddin Khalji?
x: Land was measured with the biswa as the standard unit.

s: Under Alauddin Khalji, on what was Charai levied?
x: Charai was a grazing tax on milch animals; Ghari was the house tax.

s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's revenue reforms:
1. The privileges of khuts and muqaddams were abolished.
2. Land measurement covered the whole empire.
3. Khalisa land was expanded by reclaiming milk, waqf and inam lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Intermediaries lost their privileges and khalisa grew; measurement was limited to Delhi and nearby areas.

s: Barani's causes of revolt perceived by Alauddin were noble wealth, noble marriages and gatherings, drinking and which other?
x: Barani's four causes were noble wealth, noble intermarriage and gatherings, a weak intelligence system and drinking.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of Alauddin Khalji's ordinances?
o: Confiscation of religious grants and free lands
Permission for nobles to form unrestricted marriage alliances
x: Noble marriages and gatherings required royal permission; the other three were part of his ordinances.

s: Prohibition of liquor and gambling, control of markets and severe punishment of offenders are associated with which Delhi Sultan?
x: All three measures belong to Alauddin Khalji: his ordinances prohibited liquor and gambling, he regulated the markets, and offenders were punished severely. Balban was harsh but did not control markets; Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz did not impose these measures together.

s: Which ordinance of Alauddin Khalji was aimed at nobles' intermarriages and gatherings?
o: Royal permission for feasts and marriage alliances
x: To check nobles' gatherings and intermarriage, feasts and marriage alliances needed royal permission.

s: Which one of the following best explains the contradictory effects of Alauddin Khalji’s reforms?
o: They weakened the army but eliminated all opposition among the nobles.
They raised prices and ended the use of spies, but strengthened provincial autonomy.
They benefited merchants and peasants while weakening the central government.
They kept prices low and strengthened the army, but espionage and repression generated discontent.
x: The reforms helped maintain low prices and a strong army capable of resisting the Mongols, but repression and espionage created widespread discontent.

s: With which dynasty are token currency, transfer of capital and canals associated?
x: The Tughlaqs are known for token currency, capital transfer and canals; the Khaljis for market control and the Lodis as the first Afghan dynasty.

s: Who is the main source for Alauddin Khalji's market control measures?
x: Barani is the main source; Mubarak Shah later abolished the controls.

s: Which Sultan abolished Alauddin Khalji's price controls and restored confiscated lands after ascending the throne?
x: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316–1320) abolished the price controls, restored confiscated lands and withdrew the harsh regulations.

s: In which work is Ziauddin Barani's account of Alauddin Khalji's reforms found?
x: Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, the main account of the reforms; Khazain-ul-Futuh is by Amir Khusrau.

s: Who wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh, describing Alauddin Khalji's campaigns?
x: Amir Khusrau, who went on the 1310 campaign, wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh.

s: Which was the first Afghan dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
x: The Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty; they founded Agra.

s: Which pair of Delhi Sultanate dynasty and key contribution is wrongly matched?
x: Agra was founded by the Lodis; the Tughlaqs are known for token currency, capital transfer and canals.

s: Which dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate founded Agra?
x: The Lodis, the first Afghan dynasty, founded Agra.

s: Alauddin Khalji’s reign is often called the ‘imperial period’ of the Delhi Sultanate mainly because it was marked by:
o: the replacement of the Sultanate by the Bahmani kingdom
the exclusive supremacy of the ulema over state policy
extensive conquests, strong centralisation and imperial ambitions
the abandonment of expansion and the growth of provincial independence
x: Alauddin’s extensive conquests, centralised administration, strong army and imperial ambitions led his reign to be described as the imperial period of the Sultanate.

s: The office of Ariz-i-Mamalik under Alauddin Khalji was associated principally with which department?
x: Ariz-i-Mamalik was the head of the army department. It was not a ministerial office concerned with law or religious endowments.

s: Which ruler is associated with the creation of the first standing army paid in cash, along with the systems of dagh and huliya?
x: Alauddin Khalji created the first standing army paid in cash and introduced dagh and huliya in military administration.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes dagh from huliya or chehra?
o: Dagh was the cash payment of soldiers, whereas huliya was the recruitment of cavalry.
Dagh was a land-revenue assessment, whereas huliya recorded the wealth of nobles.
Dagh was the registration of peasants, whereas huliya was the measurement of land.
Dagh was the branding of horses, whereas huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers.
x: Dagh referred to branding horses and huliya or chehra to the descriptive roll of each soldier. Neither was a land-revenue measure or an assessment of nobles’ wealth.

s: Which Bahmani minister later copied Alauddin Khalji's dagh and chehra?
x: Mahmud Gawan of the Bahmanis brought in dagh, chehra, land measurement and a larger khalisa.

s: How were the soldiers of Alauddin Khalji's standing army paid?
x: Alauddin was the first Sultan with a large permanent standing army paid in cash.

s: Which of the following Firoz Shah Tughlaq institution–function pairs is correctly matched?
o: Diwan-i-Istihqaq – Pensions and grants to deserving persons
x: Diwan-i-Istihqaq gave pensions and grants; Diwan-i-Khairat handled charity, Diwan-i-Bandagan slaves, and Dar-ul-Shifa was a free hospital.

s: What did Firoz Shah Tughlaq's Diwan-i-Bandagan deal with?
x: Diwan-i-Bandagan looked after about 1,80,000 slaves; charity was Diwan-i-Khairat.

s: What did the Diwan-i-Istihqaq of Firoz Shah Tughlaq deal with?
x: Diwan-i-Istihqaq handled pensions and grants.

s: Which Sultan of Delhi is known for laying out about 1,200 fruit gardens near Delhi?
x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq planted about 1,200 orchards near Delhi and restored 30 gardens of Alauddin.

s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq set up an employment bureau to help which of the following?
x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq opened an employment exchange to find work for the unemployed; slaves were looked after by the Diwan-i-Bandagan.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a town associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
x: Firozabad, Fatehabad and Hisar Firoza were associated with Firoz Shah. Daulatabad was the renamed capital under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

s: From which temple library did Firuz Tughlaq obtain about 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts?
x: The manuscripts came from the Jawalamukhi temple library at Nagarkot, and Azizuddin Khalid Khani translated some into Persian.

s: Which of the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's canal policy is correct?
o: He built canals mainly to connect Bengal with Sind.
He abolished irrigation charges and prohibited the construction of canals.
He built the largest number of canals among the Delhi Sultans and levied haq-i-sharb.
His canals were drawn only from the Ganga and the Narmada.
x: Firoz Shah built more canals than any other Delhi Sultan and imposed an irrigation cess called haq-i-sharb.

s: At what rate was Firoz Shah Tughlaq's irrigation cess, haq-i-sharb, levied?
x: Firoz Shah's irrigation cess, haq-i-sharb, was one-tenth of the produce. He built the largest number of canals among the Delhi Sultans.

s: From where were the Ashokan pillars brought to Delhi during the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
x: Firoz Shah transported Ashokan pillars from Topra in the Ambala region and from Meerut to Delhi.

s: Which of the following is the autobiography of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
x: Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is the autobiography of Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

s: Between which points did Firoz Shah Tughlaq's longest canal, about 150 miles long, run?
x: The Yamuna-Hisar canal (150 miles) was the longest; the Sutlej-Ghaggar canal was 96 miles.

s: Under what name was Firoz Shah's Rajabwah canal restored in Akbar's time?
x: The Rajabwah was restored under Akbar as the Shihab (Shahab) Canal.

s: What was the title of Azizuddin Khalid Khani's Persian translation of Sanskrit manuscripts from Jawalamukhi?
x: Manuscripts from the Nagarkot campaign were translated as Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi.

s: Which of the following towns was founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded Jaunpur, Firozabad, Fatehabad, Hisar Firoza and Firozpur.

s: What was the earlier name of Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was called Juna Khan (also Ulugh Khan) before he became Sultan; Ghazi Malik was his father Ghiyasuddin.

s: In which year did Muhammad bin Tughlaq transfer his capital to Devagiri?
x: The capital was transferred in 1327; token currency followed around 1329–30.

s: What did the token currency introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq around 1329-30 consist of?
o: Gold and silver coins issued to overcome a gold shortage
Silver and copper coins issued exclusively for the army
Copper and brass coins intended to function as tokens
Lead and potin coins modelled on Satavahana currency
x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced token currency in copper and brass because of a shortage of silver. Widespread forgery led to its recall and redemption at heavy cost.

s: What did Muhammad bin Tughlaq's higher taxation of the Doab, coinciding with a famine, lead to?
x: Meant to raise revenue, the Doab tax increase coincided with famine and caused peasant revolts and flight.

s: What was the aim of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Qarachil (Kumaon hills) expedition?
x: The Qarachil expedition aimed to secure the hill frontier; the Khurasan expedition aimed at Central Asian conquest.

s: How did Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Khurasan expedition end?
o: The army being destroyed in the hills
x: The army raised for Khurasan was disbanded unpaid; destruction in the hills was the fate of the Qarachil expedition.

s: What was the silver coin issued by Muhammad bin Tughlaq called?
x: MBT's silver coin was the Adli; his new gold coin was called Dinar by Ibn Battuta.

s: Which of the following pairs of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's experiment and its result is correctly matched?
o: Khurasan expedition – army destroyed in the hills
Transfer of capital – court stayed at Daulatabad
x: Token currency led to mass forgery; the Khurasan army was disbanded unpaid, the Qarachil army was destroyed and the court returned to Delhi.

s: To which country did Muhammad bin Tughlaq send Ibn Battuta, the Qazi of Delhi, as envoy in 1342?
x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta Qazi of Delhi and sent him as envoy to China in 1342.

s: Which of the following observations is associated with Ibn Battuta's account of the Delhi Sultanate?
o: Sati was permitted only to members of the royal family.
Sati was completely prohibited throughout the Sultanate.
Sati was not recorded by any contemporary traveller.
x: Ibn Battuta recorded the practice of sati and stated that it required the Sultan's permission.

s: Which of the following statements about Ibn Battuta’s Rihla is correct?
o: It was written in Arabic and describes conditions in the Sultanate and the Deccan.
It was written in Persian and deals only with Central Asia.
It was written in Hindavi and describes only Vijayanagara.
It was written in Sanskrit under the patronage of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
x: Rihla, also called Kitab-ul-Rehla, was written in Arabic and describes conditions in the Sultanate and the Deccan.

s: Who described Muhammad bin Tughlaq as a 'mixture of opposites'?
x: Barani described Muhammad bin Tughlaq as a 'mixture of opposites'. Ibn Battuta characterised him as eccentric, severe in temper and generous.

s: In whose reign did Ibn Battuta, the first foreign traveller to Vijayanagara, visit the kingdom?
