x: Ibn Battuta is identified in this context as the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara during the reign of Harihara I.

s: Where was Ibn Battuta born?
x: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta (1304-1377) was born at Tangiers.

s: Which of the following works was written by Barani?
x: Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari; Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is Firoz's autobiography.

s: Which historian remarked on the death of Muhammad bin Tughlaq that 'the king was freed from his people and they from their king'?
x: The remark is by Badauni; Barani called MBT a 'mixture of opposites'.

s: In which year did Ibn Battuta arrive in India?
x: Ibn Battuta came to India in 1333, during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign, and stayed till 1342.

s: Which post did Muhammad bin Tughlaq give to Ibn Battuta?
x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta the Qazi (judge) of Delhi.

s: Who is the author of Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi?
x: Ziauddin Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari.

s: What was the relief and cultivation camp near Kannauj on the Ganga, set up during the famine in Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign, called?
x: Swarga-dwari was a famine-relief camp on the Ganga near Kannauj, established for relief and cultivation.

s: With which of the following was the Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi of Muhammad bin Tughlaq mainly concerned?
x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was an agriculture department intended to extend cultivation, especially by bringing waste land under the plough.

s: For what were taqavi (sondhar) loans mainly given during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign?
x: Taqavi or sondhar loans were agricultural advances intended to help cultivators purchase seed and dig wells.

s: According to Ibn Battuta, at what intervals were the horse couriers (uluq) posted?
x: Horse couriers were every four miles; foot couriers (dawa) had three stations to every mile.

s: How did the 'dawa' couriers of the Sultanate postal system described by Ibn Battuta travel?
x: Dawa were foot couriers; uluq were horse couriers.

s: Which rebel was Muhammad bin Tughlaq pursuing when he died at Thatta in 1351?
x: MBT died at Thatta on the way to Sindh, chasing the rebel Taghi after a Gujarat revolt.

s: Who was the first Sultan of Delhi to dig canals?
x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq first dug canals; Firoz Shah dug the largest number.

s: Which of the following Sultan–policy pairs is correctly matched?
o: Alauddin Khalji – Token currency and capital transfer
Firoz Shah Tughlaq – Canals, irrigation and public works
Muhammad bin Tughlaq – Blood and Iron policy
x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built canals and public works; Alauddin brought market control, Balban Blood and Iron, and Muhammad bin Tughlaq token currency and the capital transfer.

s: Which of the following was NOT associated with Balban?
o: The doctrine of blood and iron
x: Branding of horses, or dagh, was a measure of Alauddin Khalji. Balban was associated with Sijda, paibos, the Zil-i-Ilahi theory and the policy of blood and iron.

s: Which one of the following pairs of a city of Delhi and its founder is correctly matched?
x: Siri was founded by Alauddin Khalji and Tughlaqabad by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq. Firoz Shah founded Firozabad, not Tughlaqabad; Balban did not found Siri; Muhammad bin Tughlaq is linked with Daulatabad.

s: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
o: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq — Revenue increase limited to about one-tenth
x: The Zil-i-Ilahi theory was associated with Balban, not Iltutmish. Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq and Firoz Tughlaq are correctly matched with the measures given.

s: For whom did Ain-ul-Mulk Multani win Malwa in 1305?
x: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani won Malwa for Alauddin in 1305 and later served MBT and Firoz.

s: With whom is the Dahsala system associated?
x: Todar Mal devised the Dahsala; Abul Fazl wrote Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari.

s: Who introduced dagh, the branding of horses?
x: Dagh was Alauddin Khalji's measure, not Balban's.

s: With which Sultan is the title Zil-i-Ilahi associated?
x: Zil-i-Ilahi was Balban's title, along with sijda and paibos.

s: Whom did Ghazi Malik kill to become Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320?
x: Ghazi Malik, earlier governor of Punjab, killed Khusrau Shah and became Sultan in 1320.

s: To about what share did Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq limit any increase in land revenue?
x: Ghiyasuddin limited any increase to about one-tenth and raised it gradually, besides drought remission and cultivation of waste land.

s: During whose reign was Warangal conquered and renamed Sultanpur?
x: Warangal fell in 1323 during Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's reign and was renamed Sultanpur.

s: In which year did Warangal fall to the Tughlaq forces after a five-month siege?
x: Juna Khan first attacked Warangal in 1321-22; it fell after a five-month siege in 1323, before Ghiyasuddin's death in 1325.

s: Where did Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq die in 1325 when a wooden pavilion collapsed?
x: He died at Afghanpur in 1325 (Ibn Battuta suspected Juna Khan); he had built Tughlaqabad.

s: Of which province was Ghazi Malik the Governor against the Mongols under Alauddin Khalji?
x: Ghazi Malik (later Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq) was Governor of Punjab under Alauddin, guarding against the Mongols.

s: Which city of Delhi was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq?
x: Ghiyasuddin built Tughlaqabad; Siri was Alauddin's and Firozabad and Hisar were Firoz's.

s: In which river did the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra II die after the fall of Warangal?
x: Prataparudra II was taken towards Delhi and died in the Narmada.

s: Which one of the following statements about Malik Maqbul is correct?
o: He established the Bahmani kingdom under the title Hasan Gangu.
He was the founder of the Madurai Sultanate and was known as Ahsan Shah.
He founded Vijayanagara jointly with Harihara and Bukka.
He was originally a captured Brahmin named Jagannatha Pandit and later became Firoz Shah's wazir.
x: Malik Maqbul was originally the captured Brahmin Jagannatha Pandit, who converted to Islam and later became Firoz Shah's wazir, Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul.

s: In which year was the Madurai Sultanate established?
x: The Madurai Sultanate dates to 1335, Vijayanagara to 1336 and the Bahmani kingdom to 1347.

s: Around which year did the Reddis expel the Tughlaq forces from coastal Andhra?
x: Coastal Andhra was freed around 1325, before the Madurai Sultanate (1335), Vijayanagara (1336) and the Bahmani kingdom (1347).

s: Under whose guidance did Harihara and Bukka found Vijayanagara?
x: Harihara and Bukka, sent by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, founded Vijayanagara under Vidyaranya's guidance.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Coastal Andhra liberation — Prolaya Vema Reddi
Musunuri recapture of Warangal — Kapaya Nayaka
x: The Bahmani kingdom was founded by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah. Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah was associated with the Madurai Sultanate.

s: For understanding which of the following are the Vilasa copper plate of Prolaya Nayaka and Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam important?
o: The conditions under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions
The revenue system of the Bahmani kingdom
The maritime trade policy of the Madurai Sultanate
The succession disputes among the Mughal emperors
x: The Vilasa copper plate and Madhura Vijayam describe the conditions prevailing under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions.

s: Who recaptured Warangal from the Tughlaqs in 1336?
x: Kapaya Nayaka of the Musunuri family, after Prolaya Nayaka, recaptured Warangal in 1336.

s:
Consider the following statements about the year 1336:
1. The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded.
2. Kapaya Nayaka recaptured Warangal.
3. The Bahmani kingdom was founded.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vijayanagara's founding and Kapaya Nayaka's recapture of Warangal both date to 1336; the Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347.

s: Who established the Madurai Sultanate?
x: Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah established the Madurai Sultanate in 1335.

s: Who founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347?
x: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu) founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347 after a revolt against Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

s: Who is the author of Madhura Vijayam, which describes Tughlaq rule in the South?
x: Madhura Vijayam was written by Gangadevi; it describes the conditions under the Madurai Sultanate and Tughlaq rule.

s: Between which years is the Tughlaq period of the Delhi Sultanate generally placed?
x: The Tughlaq period began with Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320 and ended when Khizr Khan took Delhi in 1414.

s: Who was the Tughlaq Sultan on the throne of Delhi at the time of Timur's invasion in 1398?
x: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah Tughlaq, the last Tughlaq, ruled during Timur's invasion of 1398. Firoz had died in 1388, and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq II and Abu Bakr were earlier weak successors who fought each other.

s: Who took Delhi in 1414, ending the Tughlaq period?
x: Khizr Khan took Delhi in 1414, closing the Tughlaq period (1320-1414).

s: Which of the following was one of the weak successors of Firoz Shah Tughlaq after 1388?
x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq II and Abu Bakr were weak successors after 1388; Juna Khan was Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the end of the Tughlaq dynasty?
o: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah was the last Tughlaq Sultan
Timur invaded during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
x: Timur invaded in 1398 under Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah, the last Tughlaq, not under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

s: For which of the following is Firoz Shah Tughlaq's wazir Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul noted?
o: Paying compensation to people who had suffered under Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Introducing token currency in copper and brass
Leading the Qarachil expedition into the Kumaon hills
x: Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul paid compensation to persons who had suffered during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's rule.

s: After whose death was Firoz Shah Tughlaq placed on the throne at Thatta in 1351?
x: Firoz Shah succeeded Muhammad bin Tughlaq at Thatta in 1351 and ruled until 1388.

s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq made the iqtas:
x: Firoz made iqtas hereditary; he also wrote off taqavi loans, fixed land revenue and kept the four Islamic taxes.

s: Which statement correctly describes the jizya policy of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
o: He replaced jizya with the irrigation cess haq-i-sharb.
He abolished jizya for all non-Muslims.
He made jizya a separate tax and extended it to Brahmins.
He levied jizya only on Muslim peasants.
x: Firoz Shah made jizya a separate tax and, following the advice of the ulema, extended it to Brahmins for the first time.

s: Against whom were Firoz Shah Tughlaq's two failed expeditions to Bengal sent?
x: Both Bengal campaigns against Haji Iliyas failed; Jam Babaniya of Sind agreed to pay tribute.

s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq abolished about how many taxes?
x: Firoz abolished about 24 taxes and kept only the four Islamic taxes.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four Islamic taxes retained by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
x: Firoz kept kharaj, jizya, khams and zakat; haq-i-sharb was his irrigation cess.

s: Which ruler of Sind agreed to pay tribute to Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
x: Jam Babaniya of Sind agreed to pay tribute; Haji Iliyas of Bengal resisted Firoz's two expeditions.
